chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What the people are reporting is that the prayer in congregation is superior to the prayer of a man alone by twenty-five prayers.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'They are speaking the truth.' I said, 'Do two men constitute a congregation?' He said, 'Yes, and the man stands on the right of the Imam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward difference between congregational prayer and individual prayer in Shia Islam, and how many people make a congregation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi confirms the superior merit of congregational prayer, quantifying its reward as twenty-five times that of solitary prayer, while clarifying that the minimal requirement for a Jama'ah is just two individuals. It further specifies the ritual arrangement, noting that the follower stands to the right of the Imam, a detail that underscores the structured hierarchy within the prayer formation. This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for defining the validity and spiritual weight of communal worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘What the people are reporting is that the Salāt in a Jam’at is superior to the Salāt of the man praying alone, by twenty five Salāts’. So heasws said: ‘They are speaking the truth’. So I said, ‘Can the two men happen to be (classified as) a Jam’at?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, and the man would be standing upon the right of the Imam’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’People say that performing Salah (prayer) in congregation is more virtuous than twenty-five Salah (prayer) performed alone. Is this true ? 5 The Imam replied, ‘What they say is right.’ I then asked, ‘Can two people be considered a congregation?’ He, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, said, ‘Yes, but one should stand on the right side of the prayer leader.’”
